why: Bytes an object's own code writes from a pointer's low bytes (an AI data's byte, a moved object's coordinate), read by it only as such: compared as the pointer they came from (byte k of the word at `pointer` in the same record, read as what it names), each game's objects at their own addresses. part: 'ai' an enemy's AI data by its BN5 ids; 'obj' an object of a kind and type (BN5's number, a moved type's in both records).

rules.evidence: KnightMan's state 11 (BN5's 9), its sub-state 0x10 (BN5 0x080FC08C): ldr r0,[r7,#0x28] (AttackVars +0x28: his companion's overlay, the first kind's 0x56); bl 0x080C386C (BN6 0x080C5D80, the same bytes: its +0xB cleared, r0 returned as it came); strb r0,[r7,#1] (BN5 0x080FC0AA): the phase's flag the overlay's address's low byte, tested only as nonzero (0x080FC090). The overlay in T1 slot 2 in both traces: 0xB0 in BN5, 0x60 in BN6 (0x0203A9B0 + 2 x 0xD8).

NumberMan's number box (the third kind's 0x8B, moved, its type BN5's number in both records): his state at BN5 0x080FA5A0 hands its spawner (0x080D7B54) AttackVars +0x28, a pointer to his own object's +0x68 (written at 0x080F9F64), in r3, which the third kind's spawner stores as Z (+0x3C) and the box keeps at +0x60; its init (0x080D78F2) clears Z's upper half: Z's lower half the pointer's, his object's place in each game's T1 table (numberman_v1 at t157: BN5 0xB340, BN6 0xAAF0)
